notes.title: Lite Campaign Open Beta Update 3 (B160928)
notes.notes:
We have made good progress on fixing bugs and polishing the open beta version further, getting close to a version that marks the definitive Lite Campaign V1 release as a public update.

In today's update we have a whole bunch of more fixes, among others one which makes your savegames from before work again after that unfortunately got broken with the last patch. Here are the latest changes:

[b]B160928 Improvements[/b]
[list][*] Added auto-update from 365-day year to 360-day year for savegames
[*] Added a lot of tooltips for engineering & production pages
[*] Added info about reputation/prestige preferences of demographcis[/list]
[b]B160928 Fixes[/b]
[list][*] Fixed empty demographics showing as competitive
[*] Fixed negative cars sales number prediction
[*] Fixed production split UI affecting wrong UI elements
[*] Fixed design not appearing after quitting out without sign-off
[*] Fixed yearly report prestige/reputation change
[*] Fixed several tech-pool related bugs
[*] Fixed engine reliability getting negative values
[*] Fixed cars getting better drivability the worse they become
[*] Fixed limited & mass production causing engine production mismatches
[*] Fixed specific bug in distribution window when revising project
[*] Fixes issue with not having two demographics pinned
[*] Fixed various timeline & top bar issues
[*] Fixed issue with deleting engines from productions
[*] Limited number of trims/variants to the intended limit of six
[*] Disallowed changing engine after sign-off via timeline[/list]

[b]Update on the Polls for Lite Campaign V2[/b]

Last week we asked you which two features you would most like to see out of six different options. These two options will be included in the second iteration of the Lite Campaign, V2. The two clear winners are "Simple R&D" with 63% of the votes on one side and "Engineering Familiarity" with 57% on the other side. Here just a recap of what these two options are:

[b]Simple R&D[/b] - In order to stay ahead of the curve you must invest money into R&D. The simple tech pool model into which you place points at the setup remains and acts as a lower limit from now on. Via a simple menu in the “hub area” you can continuously invest different levels of money into “tabs” of the car & engine designers, which slowly gets you more tech pool to unlock new tech or improve component quality.

[b]Engineering Familiarity[/b] - Engineering specific design choices makes them quicker to engineer thereafter, making your company an expert in specific designs after reusing them over and over, giving your company a “style” you will perfect over the years. Technology familiarity overlaps, too. For example, if you have spent a lot of time making 2-barrel carbs, then the 4-barrel carbs won’t be magic to you, but MPFI still will.

Unfortunately we cannot feasibly add engine sharing or adding facelifts, that will have to wait until the UE4 version of the game and campaign. As soon as we have released the V1 version of the Lite Campaign to the default branch here on Steam, we'll move on to implementing the two new features you chose and make more improvements and fix bugs, etc. So please keep the feedback coming!

Anyway, thank you all for your participation.
Cheers!

notes.notes:
After a longer than planned development cycle, we're happy to announce that the Lite Campaign Update is ready to launch into open beta.

notes.title: Little Dev Update & Release Schedule
notes.notes:
Alright! We're almost there. Mid next week we'll launch into Open Beta for the coming big update.

Currently we add the last few things needed for the player to have enough feedback playing the Lite Campaign to make sound decisions, as well as fixing various bugs.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8118030/5eeb429a86ad245ea00c0c2ef9cd49f6c10a3dd2.png[/img]

As we are a bit delayed with this big update, we decided to give its launch a slightly different structure. Normally we'd have a 2-3 week open beta and first after that update the public branch of the game. This time we'll do the following:

1) About one week of open beta focused only on bugfixes and or major issues.
2) After that, release the fixed version to the public branch.
3) Add more features into the Lite Campaign for about another week.
4) Run a second open beta for these new features to be tested.
5) Release that second fixed version to the public branch.
6) About one more week of bugfixing if needed.

So basically a 2-stage release of the Lite Campaign mode. We want to do that to get the new version to you as soon as possible, without cutting any features from the Lite Campaign we think are vital to enjoying it for what it is.

That we see as important as there again will be a long wait till the next update, which will be the full UE4 port of the game! :) We aim to get that to you for Christmas ;) although, you know how precise our estimates are, i.e. pretty bad!

Check out the latest Little Dev Update, which takes a look at the new sign-off screen and rambles about various development woes.
https://youtu.be/TVPRhWxGl2g
Hang in there! :)
Cheers!

notes.title: Little Dev Update: 15. July 2016
notes.notes:
After a long wait and some delay, we can show to you the first (very rough) implementation of the fundamentals of the Lite Campaign mode. There is still heaps of work to do before this is playable, but after solving some fundamental issues, things are progressing nicely.

https://youtu.be/mkYs1MH9hMg
One of these issues is the memory limitations of LuaJIT, which we annihilated with a fraction of the competitor cars put into the simplified market. For the Lite Campaign we found a decent workaround, but this means that for the proper Grand Campaign mode, or even the Lite Campaign once the proper sales model is in place, we need a smarter approach we now have some time to work out. The required calculations and amount of data connected to the market calculations is indeed massive.

Anyway, have a look at the video and expect a more steady flow of Little Dev Updates in the coming weeks leading into an open beta phase of the coming big update.

Cheers!

notes.title: Big Update Public Release (B160418)
notes.notes:
Thank you all for waiting patiently, after a long open beta phase we are now ready to push this update out to all of our players. What is in this you wonder?

[b]Main Features[/b][list][*]Engineering Projects & Engineers
[*]Factory Production & Managers
[*]V12 Turbos
[*]Spaceframe Chassis
[*]8 new car bodies, 27 new body variants in total[/list]

[b]Engineering, Engineers and Factories[/b]

You can now set up engineering projects for your cars to see if your engineering team would be able to finish that +15 quality trim you built in the next 100 years or so. Select your team of engineers with special skills to shave down those engineering months.

[img]http://discourse.automationgame.com/uploads/default/original/3X/2/d/2d4c8ddb35d8b648f576ed0ad4421ab7618b1ca6.jpg[/img]

After setting up your factory production for the new cars and engines you get an updated price estimate that with higher precision tells you how well you are actually doing in those market demographics you aimed for.


[img]http://discourse.automationgame.com/uploads/default/original/3X/8/7/8780c583e3099f80987d9d11e2a9b1bed7883f4c.jpg[/img]

[b]V12 Turbos and Spaceframe Chassis[/b]

Running a car manufacturer out of your garage with a few welders? Probably not going to have the huge monocoque chassis stamping presses... now your new option for small scale production in the early years is spaceframes, which really help making cars that are not for utility purposes only (*cough* ladder frames).

[img]http://discourse.automationgame.com/uploads/default/original/3X/c/9/c9f301ea963f654419bc0f239fd9dbafa3f9c45a.jpg[/img]

With the new V12 Turbos you get even more power you can't put down onto the road, for more fun and wheelspin at 300 km/h! 


[b]What is up next?[/b]

As you can see, the additions to the engineering and factory side of things gets us a lot closer to a potential tycoon part of the game. With the big update being released, one of the first questions always is: "what is next?". To answer that straight away: really cool stuff! Take a look at this Little Big Dev Update video which tells you all about it: 
https://youtu.be/zL8X6H2IdkA
We are stoked about what is to come to Automation the next few months! :) 
Hope you are too, but first of all, enjoy the new update.


[b]20. April Edit:[/b] We just released a little patch to address the issues some people had with the latest public build, as well as two balance changes:
[list][*]Added Prestige stat dependencies for cargo, doors, seats
[*]Rebalanced engine factory production output
[*]Fixed engine designer hold / revert functionality
[*]Fixed issue with engine size color indicator in drop-down
[*]Fixed trim year sometimes falsely defaulting to 2016
[*]Fixed 70sWedgeLarge body rear lift value[/list]Cheers!

notes.title: Big Update Public Release (B151208)
notes.notes:
With just one week of delay we come out of open beta and are ready for the main release of this big update. Below you find an overview of the main new features.


[b]Engineering Time & Tooling Costs[/b]

You now get feedback on how complex your designs are to engineer and how much the factory tooling would cost to set up. While it may seem like a small thing, this is a very important step towards the tycoon part. How quickly do you need to get your new designs onto the market again? Better check those quality sliders then, they might hurt.

[img]http://automationgame.com/media/news_151208_2.jpg[/img]


[b]V12 Engines[/b]

The prestige king among engine configurations has made its way into Automation. How about a 1.0L V12 with individual throttle bodies that revs to the moon? Or more like a 16L monster that makes 400hp at 2000 RPM? Go wild with this new configuration.

[img]http://automationgame.com/media/news_151208_1.jpg[/img]


[b]Balance Changes & Pushrod Suspensions[/b]

With the market demographics in place, a lot of exploits and balance problems have been sorted out, about 50 of them to be precise. In addition to that we now give you access to the most hypercar of suspensions: the pushrod design.


Here the list of new features waiting to be tried out in the latest public release:

[b]Main Features[/b][list][*]Added Engineering Time
[*]Added Tooling Costs
[*]Added V12 Engines
[*]Added Pushrod Suspensions
[*]All New Track Calculations
[*]Added Car Bodies & Variants[/list]
[b]Major Balance Changes[/b][list][*]Revamped tire size vs. grip model and stat effects
[*]Regions affect footprint, practicality, and safety %
[*]Rebalanced fuel system stats
[*]Rebalanced all brake related stats
[*]Changed many part unlock years 
[*]Rebalanced utility and offroad dependencies
[*]Rebalanced all car & "General" engine scenarios[/list]
[b]Other Changes[/b][list][*]Rebalanced gearbox types, gears, and gearing effects
[*]Penalize very tall first gears
[*]Penalize too slow acceleration
[*]Rebalanced market demographics
[*]Rebalanced ride height effects
[*]Rebalanced solid axles
[*]Rebalanced suspension effect on load
[*]Rebalanced seats vs. cargo & passenger space
[*]Rebalanced comfort effect of entertainment
[*]Rebalanced safety packages progression
[*]Engine bay squeeze factor now affects service costs
[*]Changed Al engine block and head effects
[*]Smoothness effect from Mg engine blocks
[*]Rebalanced mid-/rear-engine cooling
[*]Rebalanced economy calculations for idle RPM
[*]Rebalanced offroad skidpad weight
[*]Added blowoff, backfire and exhaust burble sounds
[*]Added turbo sounds to test track[/list]
...plus plenty of small fixes and additions.

Enjoy the update and keep your eyes open for the soon to follow overview of what we are going to work on next.

Cheers!

notes.title: Big Update Public Release (B151001)
notes.notes:
After a bit less than two weeks in open beta with seven bugfix updates, most things have been sorted out and we are ready for the main release of this big update. Below you find an overview of the main new features.


[b]Buyer Demographics & Market Regions[/b]

You now get direct feedback on what your car is good and how many people can afford to buy it in 60 different demographics that all have distinctly different tastes and budgets. Optimize your cars to become the most competitive throughout the game.

[img]http://www.automationgame.com/wp-content/uploads/Markets-1024x576.jpg[/img]

A first rough implementation of three different, fictional, static markets for you to try and conquer with your designs. Every region has plenty of characteristics that influence buyer choices, even in this incomplete stage of their development.


[b]Rear-Engined Cars[/b]

[img]http://www.automationgame.com/wp-content/uploads/Rear-Engined-Cars-1024x576.jpg[/img]

Finally you can put engines on or behind the rear axle of your cars, but watch out for that massive oversteer coming your way.


[b]V6 Turbo Engines & Plenty of Little Things[/b]

[img]http://www.automationgame.com/wp-content/uploads/V6-Turbos-1024x576.jpg[/img]

Wanted to put a twin-turbo system on your V6 designs? Now you can!

That is of course not the only changes to the game, there have been plenty of additions, just some of them are:
[list][*]Revamped detailed stats
[*]Added Convertibles
[*]Added a Company Manager
[*]Many new car bodies
[*]Revamped economy calculations
[*]Multithreaded car calculations
[*]New calcs for passenger & cargo sizes
[*]Much prettier Car & Engine Managers
[*]...and many more things for you to discover[/list]
A big thank you to everyone who helped find and report bugs in the open beta phase of this update cycle! In the next days we will give you news on what the next subproject will include in a Little Dev Update.

Thank you for your patience and have fun with this update.
Cheers!

notes.title: Open Beta Update 1 (B150921)
notes.notes:
The first day of fixing bugs and various issues with the first open beta release was pretty productive and now the biggest apparent issues have been sorted out. No doubt there are plenty more though! 

Thanks to all of you who have posted feedback and bug reports, that really helps to get this version closer to release quicker.

If you haven't joined the open beta yet but want to, just go to your Steam Library, right-click Automation, Properties, Betas, opt in to the open beta.

[b]Changelog for B150921[/b]
[list][*]Fixed test track 100km/h speed limit bug.
[*]Fixed acceleration graph displayed stats.
[*]Fixed loading old cars giving them pink-box disease.
[*]Fixed AWD acceleration issues.
[*]Partial fix to demographics "pins" not set for old-version cars.
[*]Pins now show in side-bar demographic fields.
[*]Fixed an issue with loading engines into cars.
[*]Fixed exception with 1+ pages of fixture variants.
[*]Changed 60s Van introduction year to 1958.
[*]Fixed Mid-Size 70s Wedge 4-Door inability to morph.
[*]Changed 80s Executive introduction year to 1985.
[*]Fixed 80s Executive Convertible morphs.
[*]Fixed 80s Exec not being tagged as softtop.
[*]Fixed 90s Huge Wagon's rear door being too small.
[*]Fixed 90s Van having incorrectly assigned materials.
[*]Fixed 2010s Swoopy Hatchback's window angle.
[*]Fixed 2010s Large Coupe (Convertible) morphs.
[*]Fixed 10s Coupe not being tagged as hardtop.
[*]Fixed 70s Mini Car having pink boxes but no cargo.[/list]

The test track bug was due to a really scared test driver, his brakes were never tested to work beyond 100 km/h, so he didn't dare drive faster than that. :P

Please have a go with the new version and keep those bug reports coming!
Cheers!

notes.title: New Flow, V6s, Steam Workshop Update (B150626)
notes.notes:
After a week in open beta, this update is now ready for release to all Steam players of Automation (standalone update comes tomorrow)! There are countless of small changes and fixes, but the most prominent additions definitely are:

[b]New Model/Trim Flow[/b]
The new UI flow of making Models and Trims allows you to make model series of cars with multiple trims of different body variants stretched over a wide range of years. The new fixture templates make possible a quick creation of a whole lineup, using a base design you craft first that for each Trim can be individually adjusted along with the morphs of the car, which now also can be carried out with fixtures on the cars.

[b]Naturally Aspirated V6 Engines[/b]
This update brings the much requested V6 engines to the game. While we do not have turbos ready for them yet (coming in the next big update!), this very compact engine configuration will help you cram some capacity into tight engine bays.

[b]Steam Workshop Integration[/b]
We have fundamentally changed how Automation handles mods and made it much more modding friendly. Via the Steam Workshop you can now subscribe to and download all kinds of car bodies and fixtures. We are looking forward to seeing a thriving modding community for the game, and don't be surprised to be contacted by us if you make awesome stuff to be included in the core game! Please note that the proper modding support and integration is optimized for the Steam version of the game.

In the next few days we will continue polishing up the update a bit more and fix any severe issues with the patch. Once that is out of the way we are finally starting to get the first tycoon aspects into the game. The first thing will be buyer demographics and their evaluation of your cars compared to the competition. Keep an eye out for progress updates posted on our YouTube channel.

Enjoy the update and all those fancy mods!

notes.title: Hotfix B150322
notes.notes:
Sorry about the mess-up with the gearing and the drum brakes, this little patch should fix both of these issues.

[b]Fixes:[/b]
[list][*]Fixed gearing bug... again, hopefully the last time!
[*]Fixed bug making you unable to fully select drum brakes
[*]Fixed which tutorials are displayed in the engine designer via "?"[/list]

When you have crashbugs or lua errors, please report them to us so that we can have a look. Always great if we can get the car and/or engine that caused the issue too!
Cheers!

notes.title: Update 150321 [Fixes & Polish & Outlook]
notes.notes:
We’ve been working hard on another big round of bugfixes and usability improvements, with more to come. For a full update on what is going on in development, have a look at our latest Little Dev Update and check out the changelog below.
https://youtu.be/-lzTDxb4QJg
[b]Fixes:[/b]
[list][*]Fixed gearing problems for 7+ gears
[*]All sliders now activate tooltip on hover
[*]Updated UI: Brakes/Aero/Interior UI layout
[*]Improved tooltip readability in general
[*]Completely revamp of engine tutorial “More Pöwer”
[*]Music should now be quiet during tutorial videos
[*]Removed “statistics” button while on test screen
[*]Added better handling of corrupt saves files
[*]Fixed emissions tool tip text coloring wrong way
[*]Fixed coloring in side-panel stats changing fuel systems
[*]Fixed score window not showing actual last stats
[*]Added tooltips for engine flow bench
[*]Added tooltip to drive type
[*]Added tooltips for body filter options
[*]Added bore tooltip for min. capacity, min. bore, valve float, etc.
[*]Added stroke tooltip for min. capacity, min. stroke, etc.
[*]Added tooltip for block config prestige
[*]Added tooltip about valve float to cam slider
[*]Changed various tooltips to say octane instead of RON
[*]New default fuel mixture 13.5:1
[*]Fixed fuel mixture tooltip
[*]Added missing manager stat reliability string
[*]Auto-choose steel rims if only list item
[*]Deselecting a turbo now selects short cast headers
[*]Centered "START" button on engine test page[/list]
[b]Content:[/b]
[list][*]Added 70’s Mini Car[/list]

[b]Please Note:[/b] Translations for the new tooltips and other text in the game is not complete yet, so you will see _missing_stings throughout the game if you play the non-english version. We will get you an update as soon as the translations are done.

Also, please report any crashes and lua errors you are getting, we want to get this into a good state before moving on to implementing new features. Thanks for being awesome!
Cheers!

notes.title: B150315 Update [Major Fixes]
notes.notes:
We’ve been working hard on pushing out an update to you with fixes to some of the major problems with the launch version of the game. The following is the changelog for this patch and the minor patch that came a day after release.

[b]Fixes:[/b]
[list][*]Fixed fullscreen Alt-Tab issues
[*]Fixed mouse UI offset bug
[*]Indirectly fixed one of the start-up crashes
[*]Fixed body selection filter functionality, it now works as you’d expect: Upon clicking an icon, all other icons in the same category are deselected. Clicking the same icon again re-selects all icons in the section. Right-clicking does the same but doesn’t toggle all icons on/off.
[*]Fixed “flow, manual testing bench” showing in manual testing mode
[*]Made tutorial subtitles area wider to stop them from cutting off
[*]Fixed a bug where you got dropped to main menu when selecting an engine family from car manager to load, it now loads any available trim
[*]Fixed graph rendering bug switching between wheels and brakes tab
[*]Added emissions tool-tip to head & valves and fixed its coloring
[*]Temp fixed spray sound issue by removing it
[*]Centered live data & track stats buttons
[*]Fixed timeline highlighting not working correctly
[*]Fixed Lua error when changing from mid engine to front engine bodies
[*]Fixed an issue if you tried to load a car where that engine variant had been deleted
[*]Fixed economy stat in side-panel colouring wrong way
[*]Fixed issue with 10’s swoopy sedan having too high center of gravity[/list]

[b]Content:[/b]
[list][*]Added 80’s large pickup body[/list]

We are aware of the gearing bug for 7+ gears and will be attacking that one next. Thank you for being awesome and hanging in there until these were fixed!
Cheers!
